Louisville volleyball to participate in inaugural AVCA Match Point event in April 2027
The University of Louisville volleyball team will compete in April's inaugural AVCA Match Point event alongside top collegiate programs. The two-day tournament aims to expand opportunities within women's volleyball through a new partnership between AVCA and Intersport.
The University of Louisville volleyball team has been selected to participate in the inaugural AVCA Match Point event, scheduled for April 10-11, 2027, at Freedom Hall in Louisville, Ky., according to an Oct. 1 announcement.
Louisville will be one of eight teams competing in the two-day tournament. Other confirmed programs include Kentucky, Nebraska, Pittsburgh, Stanford, and Wisconsin. Two additional teams will be announced at a later date. The event will use a bracketed format with each team playing three matches—two on April 10 and one on April 11. The full match schedule is expected to be released later.
AVCA Match Point marks the beginning of a formal partnership between the American Volleyball Coaches Association (AVCA) and Intersport aimed at creating new events and expanding opportunities for volleyball throughout the year. This collaboration builds on existing initiatives such as AVCA First Serve and the State Farm Volleyball Showcase.
The timing of AVCA Match Point coincides with other major volleyball events taking place in Louisville that weekend: the JVA World Challenge and JVA 18U National Championships—two significant grassroots tournaments.
"Volleyball has tremendous momentum, and our partnership with Intersport will help us build on it by creating more opportunities for athletes, coaches and fans to engage with the sport throughout the year," said Jaime Gordon, CEO of the American Volleyball Coaches Association. "AVCA Match Point is an important first step. It brings some of the best programs in the country together for meaningful spring competition and gives fans another reason to connect with our sport. We believe there is still tremendous room for volleyball to grow, and high-quality events like this help move the sport forward."
Intersport Senior Vice President Mark Starsiak said, "This partnership with the AVCA reflects our shared belief in volleyball's continued growth and the value of creating more stages for the sport's athletes and programs... Bringing elite collegiate programs and the youth volleyball community together creates a unique opportunity to deepen connections among players, coaches and fans of all ages."
